title: Fitting subscheme complement is the bounded-generator locus
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. For $r\geq0$, let $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be the $r$-th Fitting ideal sheaf of $\mathcal F$: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ with $M=\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A)$, a surjection $A^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow M$ and kernel $K$, it is the ideal generated by the $(n-r)\times(n-r)$ minors of the $(n-r)\times n$ matrices whose rows lie in $K$ (the unit ideal when $r\geq n$); these ideals do not depend on the surjection and commute with localization [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], so they glue. Let $Z_r\hookrightarrow S$ be the closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] cut out by $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)$. Then: (1) for every $S$-scheme $T$, the pullback $\mathcal F_T$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is locally generated by at most $r$ sections [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] (every point of $T$ has an open neighbourhood on which at most $r$ sections generate it) if and only if the structure morphism $T\to S$ factors through the open subscheme $S\setminus|Z_r|$; (2) for every $s\in S$ the following are equivalent: $s\notin|Z_r|$, i.e. $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)_s=\mathcal O_{S,s}$; $\mathcal F$ can be generated by at most $r$ sections on an open neighbourhood of $s$; the stalk $\mathcal F_s$ can be generated by at most $r$ elements as an $\mathcal O_{S,s}$-module.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf-affine-sections] to every surjective finite free presentation on each affine open. This proves the first conjunct without rebuilding the affine gluing argument.

Over a local ring B, a finite module with unit r-th Fitting ideal has r generators: specialize [lem-trf-affine-principal-fitting-generators] to f=1, whose multiplication kernel is zero, and transport the generators through the quotient-by-zero isomorphism. Conversely r generators define a surjection from B^r, whose r-th Fitting ideal is the unit ideal by convention; [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change](1) identifies it with that of the original presentation.

source.place: Tag 080Z, lemma-principal-fitting-ideal, specialized to f=1; Tag 07ZC, lemma-fitting-ideal-generate-locally

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood U of x. Its section module is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], so choose a finite free presentation. By [lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization], the germ map is localization at the point prime; its base-change equivalence identifies the actual module stalk with B tensor F(U), where B is the local ring at x. Apply [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change](2) and step 2. An ideal extends to the unit ideal in B exactly when it is not contained in the point prime: one direction inverts an element outside the prime, and the other uses containment of the extended prime in the maximal ideal. The affine and closed-immersion clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine] identify this condition with being off the Fitting support and with surjectivity of the ideal inclusion on stalks.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-stalk-generators-neighbourhood] to replace the stalk generator bound in step 3 by generation on a neighbourhood. This proves all pointwise equivalences, including r=0.

For g:T to S, [lem-trf-fitting-sheaf-arbitrary-pullback] supplies finite type and quasi-coherence of the actual tensor pullback and identifies its Fitting ideal with comap of the original. Mathlib IdealSheafData.support_comap identifies its support with the inverse image of the original support. Step 4 on T therefore equates local r-generation everywhere with image containment in the complement. The open-immersion lift of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] gives precisely the requested factorization; a factorization conversely has image in that complement.
